issues.legal_issue: On the death of a tenant of a non-residential building, the heirs who succeed intestate acquire tenancy rights, including the right to continue the business in the premises.
material_facts: The original tenant died intestate while occupying a non-residential building.
The deceased tenant's married daughters were among the heirs who succeeded under the law of succession.
issues.conclusion: The heirs who succeeded intestate were tenants under the Act and acquired the deceased tenant's leasehold rights, including the right to continue the business until duly evicted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(a)(2) of the U.P. Urban Building (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 defines a tenant of a non-residential building to include the deceased tenant's heirs. Read with the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, this gives the heirs who succeed intestate the tenancy rights, not merely the liability to pay rent, but also the right to continue the business until eviction in accordance with the Act. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.non_residential_tenancy_proceeding: The proceeding concerns tenancy of a non-residential building.
predicates.tenant_died_intestate: The tenant died without leaving a will governing succession to the tenancy.
predicates.heirs_succeeded: The deceased tenant's heirs succeeded to the tenancy under the applicable law of succession.
predicates.heirs_acquire_tenancy_rights: The heirs who succeeded acquire the tenancy rights, including the right to continue the business until duly evicted.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a non-residential tenancy and the tenant died intestate leaving heirs who succeeded to the tenancy, those heirs acquire the tenancy rights, including the right to continue the business until duly evicted.

issues.legal_issue: Non-joinder of heirs who have implicitly surrendered their inherited tenancy rights does not invalidate eviction proceedings against the remaining occupants.
material_facts: The eviction proceedings concerned a non-residential building and were brought against the deceased tenant's sons and widow.
One son occupied the premises and conducted the business after the original tenant's death.
The married daughters did not participate in or claim an interest in the business conducted by that son, and they lived elsewhere with their husbands.
The Rent Appellate Tribunal found that the daughters had, by necessary implication, surrendered their inherited tenancy rights by failing to assert them after the original tenant's death.
issues.conclusion: Because the married daughters had implicitly surrendered their inherited tenancy rights, their non-joinder did not vitiate the eviction action or its maintainability.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(a)(2) of the U.P. Urban Building (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, heirs of a deceased tenant of a non-residential building are tenants and may succeed to tenancy rights. However, on the facts found by the Rent Appellate Tribunal, the daughters had implicitly surrendered their rights by not asserting them; their non-joinder therefore did not make them necessary parties whose absence invalidated the eviction proceedings. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and heirs_inherited_tenancy_rights and heirs_did_not_assert_rights and heirs_did_not_participate_in_business and heirs_lived_elsewhere and remaining_occupant_ran_business

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction of occupants from a rented building.
predicates.heirs_inherited_tenancy_rights: The deceased tenant's heirs inherited tenancy rights in the building.
predicates.heirs_did_not_assert_rights: The heirs did not assert their inherited tenancy rights after the tenant's death.
predicates.heirs_did_not_participate_in_business: The heirs did not participate in or claim an interest in the business conducted from the premises.
predicates.heirs_lived_elsewhere: The heirs lived elsewhere with their spouses.
predicates.remaining_occupant_ran_business: An occupant against whom eviction was sought remained in the premises and conducted the business there.
predicates.nonjoinder_does_not_invalidate_ejectment: The heirs' non-joinder does not invalidate or defeat the eviction action.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding, where heirs inherited tenancy rights but did not assert them or participate in the business, lived elsewhere, and another occupant continued the business, their non-joinder does not invalidate the eviction action.
